hints: Integrate to obtain a tangent term in $y$ and a logarithmic term in $\cos x$.
Use $x=0$, $y=\pi/4$ to fix the constant, then substitute $y=\pi/3$.
Solve for the admissible $x$ in $0\le x<\pi/2$ and round only the final value.
walkthrough:
Separate the variables $x$ and $y$ in $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = 4\cos^2 y\tan x$:
$$\dfrac{1}{\cos^2 y}\,\mathrm{d}y = 4\tan x\,\mathrm{d}x \implies \sec^2 y\,\mathrm{d}y = 4\tan x\,\mathrm{d}x$$

Integrate both sides with respect to their variables:
$$\int \sec^2 y\,\mathrm{d}y = \int 4\tan x\,\mathrm{d}x$$

Evaluate the left-hand integral:
$$\int \sec^2 y\,\mathrm{d}y = \tan y$$

Evaluate the right-hand integral using $\tan x = \dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}$:
$$\int 4\tan x\,\mathrm{d}x = -4\ln(\cos x) = 4\ln(\sec x)$$

Write down the general solution with constant of integration $c$:
$$\tan y = -4\ln(\cos x) + c$$

Substitute the initial condition $x = 0$ when $y = \dfrac{1}{4}\pi$ to find $c$:
$$\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = -4\ln(\cos 0) + c \implies 1 = -4\ln(1) + c \implies c = 1$$

State the particular solution to the differential equation:
$$\tan y = 1 - 4\ln(\cos x) \quad \left(\text{or } \tan y = 4\ln(\sec x) + 1\right)$$

Substitute $y = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi$ into the solution and solve for $x$:
$$\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = 4\ln(\sec x) + 1 \implies \sqrt{3} = 4\ln(\sec x) + 1$$
$$4\ln(\sec x) = \sqrt{3} - 1 \implies \ln(\sec x) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{4} \approx 0.183013$$

Express in terms of $\cos x$ and exponentiate:
$$\ln(\cos x) = -\dfrac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{4} \approx -0.183013$$
$$\cos x = \mathrm{e}^{-0.183013} \approx 0.83276$$

Calculate $x = \cos^{-1}(0.83276)$ in radians in the range $0 \le x < \dfrac{1}{2}\pi$:
$$x \approx 0.5866 \implies x = 0.587 \quad \text{(to 3 significant figures)}$$
